notable_absence.finding: No capella-role gate and no exclusion of cluster access credentials - the exact inverse of ALTER BUCKET/ALTER GROUP/ALTER USER in this batch. ALTER SEQUENCE lives entirely in the data-plane credential-type-keyed privilege track.

cross_component_finding: This is the clearest confirmation in the batch that the credential-type-keyed privilege pair (Basic/Advanced) generalizes beyond the collections/index examples already in the registry to a new object family entirely (sequences), each with its own Advanced-credential privilege name ('Query Manage Sequences') following the same 'Query Manage <Noun>' naming convention as the already-catalogued 'Query Manage Index' server-RBAC privilege and 'privilege:capella-advanced-access-query-index' - reinforcing that this is a systematic per-object-type privilege scheme, not a one-off.
